name: Transponder circuit
description: A small radio module in an aluminium tray: a green board with a shielded section, chips and an antenna socket. It picks up a signal and sends it on again. Useful in building radio gear.
notes: A 120 by 80 mm tray 24 mm tall, open on top so the board shows, with the coax socket on the front edge. No aluminium finish exists, so metal-silver draws the tray.

name: Tree spile
description: A short steel spout with a hook under it. Tapped into a hole drilled in a maple, it drips sap into a bucket hung from the hook, from late winter into spring.
notes: An 80 mm galvanised tube, 12 mm across at the head, a stop collar, then a tapering spout; the bucket hook hangs under the head. CHECK VOLUME (x0.41): the reference's 50 ml is generous for so slim a part. The makeshift spile rides on this model; a cut-down pipe looks much the same at this size.

name: Rugged USB drive
description: A thumb drive sealed inside a knurled steel capsule with a screw cap and a key ring. It holds software and survives being stepped on.
notes: A 62 mm stainless capsule 17 mm across with flush knurl bands, a rubber seal at the cap joint and a small split ring at the tail; the plug sits under the cap. The two data variants are the same drive with records on it, so they share this model; their names need writing when they are drafted for a quest.

name: Willow bark
description: A curled strip of bark peeled from a willow, grey and furrowed outside and pale inside. It can be boiled down for a pain remedy.
notes: A 262 by 90 mm sheet 7 mm thick, curled across its width, with five dark furrows along it. CHECK VOLUME (x1.89): the box counts the air under the curl. bark draws the outside, which reads browner than willow; a grey bark finish would suit it better.

name: Steel wire
description: A loose coil of stiff steel wire, twist-tied to keep it together. Good for binding, mending and making small parts.
notes: About 6 m of wire in a 150 mm coil of six turns, tied in two places, one end sticking out. The wire is drawn 3 mm thick so it holds up at the 2 mm grain. CHECK VOLUME (x5.28): the reference counts the steel; the box counts the open middle of the coil.

name: Barbed wire
description: A coil of galvanised wire studded with four-point barbs. Strung across a gap, it slows anything that tries to push through.
notes: Three turns 220 mm across with fourteen barbs. CHECK VOLUME (x2.97): the box counts the open middle of the coil.

name: Steel mesh
description: A 15 cm square of fine woven steel mesh. Works as a filter, a strainer or a small screen.
notes: A 152 mm square drawn as wires every 10 mm with open squares, so the floor shows through; real filter mesh is finer than the 2 mm grain can show. CHECK VOLUME (x15.4): the reference's 6 ml is the steel alone; the box counts the open weave and the sheet's area.

name: Koji rice parcel
description: Cooked rice wrapped in corn husk, split open along the top where white and yellow-green mould has spread through it. Take it apart to recover the mould culture for brewing and fermenting.
notes: A 140 mm husk parcel tied at both ends with a split along the top showing the rice and mould patches. CHECK VOLUME (x2.37): the box counts the flared husk ends. Taking it apart into a culture item has no content field yet.
